answer: An agent economy can require diverse-cluster endorsement before an identity can trade: it must collect attestations from peers in several unrelated clusters, not just one tight grove of mutual friends. A single thread of approvals from the same circle is discounted, while a mirror check compares endorser sets of suspicious accounts — overlapping sets reveal one operator behind many faces. An attacker must therefore infiltrate many independent communities, each demanding genuine interaction, so forging a convincing identity costs far more than spawning cheap copies.
